svg.title: Cleaning the garage door photo-eye sensors — three steps
svg.desc: A pair of photo-eye sensors near the floor of a garage door. Step 1 shows where they live, step 2 a microfibre wipe, step 3 the alignment check.

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: ~ 6 inches off the floor, one each side of the door.

g.text: Dry microfibre. No window cleaner, no spray on the lens.

g.text: Spray cleaner directly. Wipe the lens with a wet cloth — the housing isn't sealed.

g.text: Both should be solid (not blinking). If green blinks, they're misaligned.

g.text: Green blinks / no LED at all

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Nudge the sensor head gently with one finger.

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Watch for solid. If it won't hold, call us.

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Vancouver fog season (Oct–Feb) is when this becomes a weekly job. Dirty lenses mimic an obstacle and the opener auto-reverses every time you try to close it.
